sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows how to justify a modelling choice.

items.prompt: AB = 4 maps to DE = 12, BC = 5. Find EF.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Decide what the quantities are before you compute anything.

items.prompt: In a right triangle, the altitude to the hypotenuse divides it into segments of length 6 and 96. Find the altitude.
A 4 m pole casts a 3 m shadow. At the same moment a building casts a 6 m shadow. How tall is the building?
A line parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two sides proportionally. Which statement correctly justifies it?
choices: The two parts of each side are congruent because the line is parallel.
The result follows from the Pythagorean theorem applied twice.
The parallel line creates corresponding angles, giving a smaller triangle similar to the original by AA, so the sides are in proportion.
The parallel line bisects both sides by definition.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Plan in writing: what you will model, why that model, and how you will check it.

items.prompt: Triangle ABC is similar to triangle DEF. Side AB = 5 corresponds to DE = 10. If BC = 8, find EF.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
